title: Integrable multi-species SSEP with reactive particle species
authors: Mathieu Dabrowski, Loïc Poulain d'Andecy, Eric Ragoucy
abstract: We investigate integrable exclusion Markov processes constructed from set-theoretical solutions of the Yang-Baxter Equation (YBE) that generalise the multi-species Symmetric Simple Exclusion Process (SSEP). We first introduce the process called the $ (p,1) $-SSEP that is analogous to the multi-species SSEP but with an extra particle species qualified as reactive. Reactive species are able to evaporate and condensate by pairs or to transform by pairs depending on the interpretation. We provide a full combinatorial study of the sectors in the periodic case. We prove the integrability of the process in the periodic case and in the open case for two types of boundaries that we introduce using Baxterisations of solutions of the reflection equation. Next we move on to the process called $ (p,q) $-SSEP, i.e. the multi-species SSEP with an arbitrary number of reactive particle species. We prove its integrability in the periodic case and, for the open case, we introduce integrable boundaries generalising the ones considered for the $ (p,1) $-SSEP. Finally, we define physical quantities relevant to the models and we compute them in the non-equilibrium stationary state of the open $ (p,q) $-SSEP for one type of integrable boundaries.
summary: This paper develops the mathematical framework for multi-species Symmetric Simple Exclusion Processes incorporating reactive particles. By leveraging techniques from integrable systems theory (YBE), the authors prove the model's integrability and derive detailed combinatorial formulas to count the system's stationary state sectors. This work provides deep theoretical insights into non-equilibrium statistical mechanics models with chemical reaction dynamics.
main_problem: The research investigates integrable multi-species Symmetric Simple Exclusion Processes (SSEP) that incorporate reactive particle species, generalizing standard SSEPs.
main_result: Integrability is proven for the general $(p, q)$-SSEP in the periodic case and for specific boundary conditions in the open case. Furthermore, explicit combinatorial formulas are derived for counting the sectors of the system's stationary state.
method: The authors employ methods rooted in quantum integrable systems theory, specifically using set-theoretical solutions to the Yang-Baxter Equation (YBE) to construct the Markov matrix and prove integrability via transfer matrices.
model_or_system: The model is the $(p, q)$-SSEP on a 1D lattice, which describes interacting particles where some species are 'reactive' and can undergo pair transformations or evaporation/condensation. The dynamics are governed by a continuous-time Markov process defined on the configuration space.
key_observables: Non-equilibrium stationary state (NESS) physical quantities, including mean lattice currents, particle densities, and reaction rates.
important_parameters: The number of singlet species ($p$), the number of reactive pairs ($q$), and the system size $L$.
main_assumptions: Integrability is assumed or proven using YBE solutions; calculations for physical quantities are performed assuming specific integrable boundary types.

paper_structure: The paper progresses by first introducing the generalized model ($(p, q)$-SSEP) and proving its integrability. It then details the analysis of the $(p, 1)$-SSEP, providing physical interpretations (evaporation vs. reaction) and deriving invariants for characterizing sectors in the periodic case before tackling open boundary conditions.
why_interesting: The connection between integrable quantum field theory structures (YBE solutions) and non-equilibrium statistical mechanics models like SSEPs is highly relevant to understanding complex many-body dynamics far from equilibrium, which is a key area of modern condensed matter physics.
